[USER] User asked for an overview of the history of rap music and its various sub-genres.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Rap music originated in African-American communities in the Bronx, New York City, in the late 1970s.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The genre was characterized by rhythmic speaking of verses over a beat, often dealing with social and political themes, including poverty, inequality, and racism.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1980s, rap music became more mainstream and commercially successful, with artists like Run DMC and LL Cool J leading the way.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1980s also saw the emergence of sub-genres like gangsta rap and conscious rap.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 1990s, the rise of West Coast hip-hop included artists like N.W.A and Tupac Shakur, and Southern rap emerged with artists like Scarface and Master P.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The 1990s also saw the birth of alternative hip-hop, incorporating elements of other genres like rock and jazz.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In the 2000s and 2010s, rap music evolved with sub-genres like crunk, snap music, and trap music, characterized by heavy use of 808 drum machines and synthesizers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other notable sub-genres include drill music and mumble rap.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Overall, rap music has become one of the most popular genres in the world, with a rich and diverse history.
